extracted.intended_audience: biomedical researchers, journal editors, peer reviewers, and research integrity professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and prescriptive guidance about identifying, characterizing, and preventing 'spin' — the misrepresentation or distortion of research — in biomedical journal articles. Focuses on practices of misreporting (e.g., beautification of methods) and misinterpretation of results and points to standards and ways to avoid such distortions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spin (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Spin has been defined as a specific intentional or unintentional reporting that fails to faithfully reflect the nature and range of findings and that could affect the impression the results produce in readers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat 'spin' as any reporting practice (intentional or not) that distorts the faithful presentation of findings and may change readers' impressions; use this definition when evaluating the fidelity of a manuscript's reporting and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misreporting by 'beautification' of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices of misreporting that involve 'beautification' of methods — presenting methods as better or more rigorous than they actually were.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate method sections for overstated rigor or omitted limitations; ensure methods are reported transparently and honestly rather than 'beautified.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Misreporting by misinterpreting the results
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms of misreporting that arise from misinterpreting study results (overclaiming, overstating implications, or drawing conclusions not supported by the data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether conclusions accurately reflect the range and strength of the evidence (e.g., avoid causal language for observational data, avoid broad claims unsupported by results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spin in reporting and interpretation of nonsignificant primary outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific problematic pattern where randomized controlled trials with statistically nonsignificant results for primary outcomes are reported or interpreted in a way that implies benefit or positive findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When primary outcomes are nonsignificant, avoid reframing secondary/surrogate findings or subgroup analyses as proof of efficacy; evaluate whether the manuscript transparently reports primary outcome results and their correct interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing potential effects of spin on readers and dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that spin can affect readers' interpretation and the dissemination of research findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider not only factual accuracy but also the likely impression created by wording, abstracts, headlines, and press materials; evaluate whether phrasing could mislead nonexpert readers or media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to ethical principles for research reporting (Declaration of Helsinki)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical principles for medical research involving human subjects as a standard informing responsible reporting and publication practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reporting complies with accepted ethical standards (e.g., honest reporting of methods and results, participant protections, transparency about harms and limitations) as articulated in ethical guidance like the Declaration of Helsinki.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reporting and transparency standards (EQUATOR / Responsible research publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to international standards and resources (e.g., EQUATOR Centre, 'Responsible research publication: International standards for authors') aimed at promoting quality and transparency in reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply established reporting guidelines (CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, etc., via EQUATOR) and author standards to prevent spin — e.g., preregistration, complete methods and results reporting, clear statements of limitations and conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and taxonomy of practices of spin
rubrics_metrics.description: The article reports various practices of spin across a spectrum from misreporting methods to misinterpreting results, and provides data on prevalence of some forms in specific fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating manuscripts, use a taxonomy of spin practices (e.g., selective reporting, selective emphasis, inappropriate extrapolation, linguistic framing) to systematically identify and document instances of distortion; consult empirical data on prevalence to prioritize common issues.
